idiom_name: class ServiceProxy < SimpleDelegator with intercepted methods spelled out
implementation_notes: Ruby's standard library already contains the proxy: SimpleDelegator forwards every method it does not itself define to the object it wraps, while definitions in the subclass stay authoritative, so equivalence costs one super call and only the intercepted operations are written out (Delegator is the same mechanism with an explicit target). A hand-written method_missing plus respond_to_missing? is the dependency-free equivalent, and Forwardable generates an explicit, fail-loudly surface when default forwarding is too permissive.
code_sketch:
require 'delegate'
class ServiceProxy < SimpleDelegator
  def now = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)

  def call(request)                       # intercepted member only
    started = now
    super(request)                        # forwarded to the subject
  ensure
    Metrics.observe('call', now - started)
  end
end
# ServiceProxy.new(real_service) delegates everything else to it
pitfalls: SimpleDelegator forwards anything you do not define, so a typo in an intercepted method name silently delegates instead of raising NoMethodError.
respond_to? and respond_to_missing? must stay consistent with the delegated surface or duck-typing checks and frameworks misclassify the proxy.
method_missing sits in every stack trace and makes is_a?-style reasoning confusing; keep the forwarded surface documented and errors explicit.

variants.name: Forwardable-generated explicit forwarders
variants.implementation_notes: When only part of the service may be exposed, Forwardable generates exactly the members you list as real methods (def_delegators :@service, :health, :status), so the proxy's surface is explicit, greppable and fails loudly on typos, while intercepted members are ordinary definitions. A hand-written method_missing plus respond_to_missing? is the equivalent without the standard library and remains the right choice when the forwarded set is computed at runtime.
variants.code_sketch:
require 'forwardable'
class ServiceProxy
  extend Forwardable
  def_delegators :@service, :health, :status   # explicit, fail-loudly surface
  def initialize(service) = @service = service
  def call(request)                            # intercepted member only
    started = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    @service.call(request)                     # same contract
  ensure
    Metrics.observe('call', Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - started)
  end
end
pitfalls: def_delegators does not follow the service: every new member must be added by hand, which is both the point of the explicit list and its maintenance cost.
Dynamic method_missing forwarding must also define respond_to_missing?, otherwise reflection, test doubles and frameworks behave inconsistently.
Keyword arguments must be forwarded as keywords (ruby2_keywords or an explicit **kwargs forwarder); a plain *args forwarder breaks keyword-heavy signatures.
